title: PRO Veterans Act of 2025
official_title: To protect regular order for budgeting for the Department of Veterans Affairs, and for other purposes.
likelihoodReason: Enacted as Public Law 119-33 on August 14, 2025. Per the printed legislative history for S. 423, the Senate considered and passed the measure on April 8, 2025 and the House considered and passed it on July 21, 2025.
summary: Enacts two Department of Veterans Affairs administrative reforms in a single Act. Section 1 (the "Protecting Regular Order for Veterans Act of 2025") requires the Secretary of Veterans Affairs to provide quarterly, in-person briefings to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs and Appropriations Committees on the VA's budget and any shortfall the Department may be experiencing, beginning the first quarter after enactment and continuing until the date that is 3 years after enactment; when a shortfall is reported, the Secretary must also present plans to address or mitigate it (a "shortfall" is defined as appropriations required to meet all statutory obligations exceeding the amount requested in the President's budget under 31 U.S.C. 1105(a)). Section 1(c) amends 38 U.S.C. 706(d) by adding a new paragraph (7): a critical skill incentive under paragraph (1) may not be provided to a Senior Executive Service (SES) employee (or comparable senior-level position, as defined by the Secretary) whose position is at the VA Central Office — including the Veterans Health Administration, Veterans Benefits Administration, and National Cemetery Administration — regardless of where the employee actually performs the functions of the position; for SES employees not at Central Office, incentives may only be provided on an individual basis (not to a group) and only with approval from a specified list of officers (Under Secretary for Benefits, Health, or Memorial Affairs; Assistant Secretary for Human Resources and Administration; Director of the Office of Management or CFO; Assistant Secretary for Accountability and Whistleblower Protection; General Counsel; and such other officers as the Secretary determines appropriate). For an SES employee whose position is primarily at Central Office but who performs some job function at other VA facilities, the employee is not considered a Central Office employee for the non-Central-Office portion of their job, and any critical skill incentive for that portion must be proportionate to the time spent at those facilities. The Secretary must submit an annual report to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs Committees on SES employees who received critical skill incentives; reports may be incorporated into other required reports. Section 2 (the "Improving Veterans' Experience Act of 2025") adds new section 325 to chapter 3 of title 38, U.S.C., establishing the Veterans Experience Office within the Department under the Office of the Secretary, headed by a Chief Veterans Experience Officer appointed by and reporting directly to the Secretary. The Office's functions include carrying out customer experience initiatives; requiring other VA offices to report regularly on customer experience metrics and improvement efforts; collecting veteran-derived data on satisfaction and usage; providing strategic guidance for engagement; and assessing and advising on VA websites and customer service. The Chief Veterans Experience Officer must submit an annual summary to the Secretary, who must submit an annual analysis to Congress within 180 days of receiving that summary, including customer service data and satisfaction data disaggregated by benefit or service and by relevant demographic categories (with potential non-use reasons such as eligibility, lack of awareness, and barriers of technology, information, or time). The Office's information must exclude personally identifiable information unless the individual consents; funds from other VA organizations may be available to reimburse the Office at cost-recovery rates when the Secretary determines contributing will not undermine those organizations' ability to provide required services; nothing in the subsection authorizes an increase in the Department's overall full-time-employee count. The Office is subject to the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a). Section 325's requirements and authorities terminate on September 30, 2028. Section 2(c) requires the Comptroller General to complete, not later than 540 days after enactment, an analysis of the methodology, effectiveness, and implementation of veteran and beneficiary customer-experience findings and feedback used by VA (including through "trust-scores," VSignals, and related survey and data-collection activities), and submit a report on the findings to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs Committees.
brief: Signed as Public Law 119-33 on August 14, 2025 — requires quarterly in-person VA budget-and-shortfall briefings to four congressional committees for 3 years, restricts VA Senior Executive Service critical skill incentives at Central Office, and establishes a Veterans Experience Office headed by a Chief Veterans Experience Officer (sunset September 30, 2028) with a GAO review due 540 days after enactment.

sections.label: Section 1 — Protecting Regular Order for Veterans

items.main: Names the section the "Protecting Regular Order for Veterans Act of 2025" or the "PRO Veterans Act of 2025" (subsection (a); 38 U.S.C. 101 note).

Requires the VA Secretary to provide quarterly, in-person briefings to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs Committees and House and Senate Appropriations Committees on the VA budget and any shortfall the Department may be experiencing, beginning the first quarter after enactment and continuing until 3 years after enactment. When a shortfall is reported, the Secretary must present plans to address or mitigate it. "Shortfall" is defined as an amount of appropriations required by the Department for a fiscal year to meet all statutory obligations that exceeds the appropriations requested in the President's budget under 31 U.S.C. 1105(a).

Amends 38 U.S.C. 706(d) by adding new paragraph (7): a critical skill incentive under paragraph (1) may not be provided to an SES employee (or comparable senior-level position, as defined by the Secretary) whose position is at the VA Central Office (including VHA, VBA, and NCA), regardless of where the employee actually performs the functions.
items.detail: Subsection (c); the Central-Office bar is in new subparagraph (A) of paragraph (7).

items.main: For SES employees not at Central Office, critical skill incentives may only be provided (i) on an individual basis (not to a group) and (ii) upon approval from a specified list of officers (or those in acting capacity): the Under Secretary for Benefits, Under Secretary for Health, or Under Secretary for Memorial Affairs; the Assistant Secretary for Human Resources and Administration; the Director of the Office of Management or the Chief Financial Officer; the Assistant Secretary for Accountability and Whistleblower Protection; the General Counsel; and such other officers as the Secretary determines appropriate.
items.detail: New 38 U.S.C. 706(d)(7)(B)(i) — enumerates the six approving-officer categories.

items.main: For an SES employee primarily at Central Office but performing some job function at other VA facilities, the employee is not treated as a Central Office employee with respect to the non-Central-Office portion, and any critical skill incentive for that portion must be proportionate to the time spent at those facilities.

Annual report requirement: not later than 1 year after enactment and annually thereafter, the Secretary must submit to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs Committees a report on SES employees who were provided a critical skill incentive; reports may be incorporated into other congressionally mandated reports to those committees.

sections.label: Section 2 — Establishment of Veterans Experience Office

items.main: Names the section the "Improving Veterans' Experience Act of 2025" (subsection (a); 38 U.S.C. 101 note).

Adds new section 325 to chapter 3 of title 38, U.S.C., establishing the Veterans Experience Office within the Department under the Office of the Secretary. The head is the Chief Veterans Experience Officer, appointed by the Secretary from among individuals the Secretary considers qualified, reporting directly to the Secretary, and responsible for carrying out the functions of the Office.

Functions include: carrying out key customer experience initiatives (setting strategy, framework, policy, and other guidance for the Department, and ensuring coordination and non-duplication with other VA activities); requiring other VA organizations to report regularly on customer experience metrics, action plans, and other improvement efforts; collecting veteran-derived data to determine satisfaction and usage of benefits and services, to be considered during policymaking; providing strategic guidance and strategies for engaging with veterans and beneficiaries, including those not using benefits and services; assessing and advising the Secretary on the accuracy and helpfulness of VA websites and other customer-facing information; and assessing and advising on VA customer service efforts.

Reporting: Each year, the Chief Veterans Experience Officer must submit to the Secretary a summary of the data received under subsection (c)(2). Each year, not later than 180 days after the Secretary receives that summary, the Secretary must submit to Congress an annual summary and analysis. Annual summaries must include customer service and experience feedback data disaggregated by benefit or service (and by relevant demographic data), and satisfaction/usage data (disaggregated similarly) including potential reasons for not using benefits (eligibility; lack of knowledge or awareness; barriers of technology, information, or time; other related reasons) and an analysis of how such reasons may be addressed.

Staff and resources: the Secretary must ensure the Office has the necessary staff, resources, and access to customer service and experience information; information must exclude personally identifiable information of individual veterans, survivors, dependents, or other beneficiaries unless the individual provides appropriate consent. Funds available for basic pay and administrative expenses of other VA organizations may be used to reimburse the Office at cost-recovery rates for services provided to those organizations if the Secretary determines that contributing will not undermine those organizations' ability to provide required services. Nothing in the subsection authorizes an increase in the number of full-time employees otherwise authorized for the Department. The Office is subject to the Privacy Act of 1974 (5 U.S.C. 552a).
Sunset: the requirements and authorities of new section 325 terminate on September 30, 2028.
items.detail: New 38 U.S.C. 325(g). A clerical amendment adds "325. Veterans Experience Office." to the table of sections at the beginning of chapter 3 of title 38.

items.main: GAO review: not later than 540 days after enactment, the Comptroller General must complete an analysis of the methodology, effectiveness, and implementation of veteran and beneficiary customer-experience findings and feedback used by VA — including the Veterans Experience Office — through "trust-scores," VSignals, and related survey and data-collection activities. The Comptroller General must submit a report of the findings to the House and Senate Veterans' Affairs Committees.

gaps: The Act does not describe consequences if the Secretary fails to provide a quarterly briefing or misses a report deadline.

The Act does not authorize additional appropriations for the Veterans Experience Office or the shortfall-mitigation plans — the Office is subject to a no-FTE-increase constraint and reimbursement-at-cost mechanism only.
The Act does not specify the criteria the Secretary uses to designate positions comparable to Senior Executive Service for purposes of the critical skill incentive restrictions.
The Act does not describe how the Veterans Experience Office's activities are to continue (or be transferred) after the September 30, 2028 sunset.
